# What words mean, one line a kind (noun, verb...): WORD <tab> KIND <tab> MEANING [<tab> BASE WORD].
# Dotterel's own short definitions, WordNet 3.0 (Princeton University, LICENSE-meanings), GCIDE for the rest.
the	article	used before a noun when it is clear which one you mean
to	preposition	towards a place, person or time; also used before a verb (to go, to eat)
and	conjunction	joins two words or parts of a sentence
of	preposition	belonging to, made from, or part of something
a	article	used before a singular noun when you mean any one, not a particular one
in	preposition	inside something, or during a period of time
I	pronoun	the person speaking or writing

on	preposition	touching the top surface of something; also about a day or date
with	preposition	together with someone or something; using something
this	determiner	the one here or now, near the speaker
was	verb	the past of "be" with I, he, she, it

as	conjunction	in the same way; also while, or because

he	pronoun	a man, boy or male animal already mentioned
not	adverb	used to make a word or sentence negative

my	determiner	belonging to me
